title: Apply an already-existing label
description: Closes an evidence gap left by labels-due-date-combo, which only tests the just-created-label path (agent creates the label and immediately carries its fresh id forward). This scenario seeds the label ahead of time via `setup`, so the agent must find-then-apply an already-existing label it does not already have the id for -- the harder path the parked label-ensure composite was evaluated against. RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-25 (netadvanced/vikunja-mcp#28 C1): optimalCallCount reasoning -- create-project (1) + bulk-create 3 tasks (1) + apply-label (1) = 3. Two equally-cheap 3-call paths now exist for the last step: (a) look up the existing label's id (e.g. vikunja_labels list --search) then bulk-create the 3 tasks with that numeric id in `labels`, or (b) bulk-create the 3 tasks first, then ONE apply-label call with `taskIds` (all 3) and `labelTitles: ["{{prefix}}existing-tag"]` (PR #178 -- ensureLabelByTitle resolves-and-reuses the already-seeded label by title, no separate lookup needed). Either way the floor is 3, unchanged from before PR #178 -- taskIds gives a *different*, equally-optimal route, not a cheaper one, since the per-task loop it replaces was never on the optimal path to begin with (a single lookup + one bulk-create-with-numeric-id call was already 3).
promptTemplate: There is already a label called "{{prefix}}existing-tag" in this Vikunja instance. Create a project called "{{prefix}}Existing Label Project" with 3 tasks, and apply the existing "{{prefix}}existing-tag" label (do not create a new label) to all 3 tasks.
